fa.name: TSMC Fab 20, Baoshan (Hsinchu)
fa.capacity: N2 node output reported at about 20,000 wafers per month in July 2026 (node-wide figure per report title; not split by fab)
fa.notes: TSMC's technology page states N2 entered volume production in Q4 2025 as planned (per search summary); coverage names Fab 20 and Fab 22 as the N2 sites. Ramp and yield figures in Taiwanese media vary and are not recorded.

fa.name: TSMC Fab 22, Kaohsiung
fa.technology: N2 (2 nm class); site originally planned for 7 nm and 28 nm before conversion (per report)
fa.notes: First N2 wafers and trial production reported Oct 2025. AFP coverage of TSMC's Dec 2025 mass-production statement names Fab 22 as an N2 site; a per-phase production date is not recorded here until a source states it. A Tom's Hardware roadmap lists phase 1 ramping and phases 2–3 to ramp in 2H 2026; TrendForce reported all five phases expected by Q4 2027 (plans, not milestones).

fa.name: TSMC Arizona second fab (Fab 21 phase 2), Phoenix
fa.notes: Apr 2026 earnings call: construction completed, 3 nm, volume production 2H 2027. Oct 2026 call: tool move-in and installation under way; volume production 3Q 2027, slightly ahead of the previous schedule (per coverage). The April item is recorded at its report date as the construction stage; completion is in the note. Phase 1 is FAC-000014.

fa.name: UMC Fab 12i Phase 3, Singapore
fa.capacity: Total UMC Singapore capacity to exceed 1 million wafers a year once phase 1 runs (per DIGITIMES)
fa.notes: First tool move-in 21 May 2024. Mass production was moved from mid-2025 to early 2026 after customer order adjustments (per Taipei Times). Opening ceremony April 2025; first-phase production scheduled for 2026 (per DIGITIMES). Start of production not confirmed in reviewed sources.

fa.name: VSMC 300 mm fab, Tampines, Singapore
fa.capacity: 44,000 300 mm wafers per month by 2029 stated at the Sept 2026 opening; 55,000 per month in 2029 stated at the Dec 2024 groundbreaking (figures differ)
fa.technology: 130 nm to 40 nm: mixed-signal, power management, analog; interposers
fa.notes: Grand opening 28 Sept 2026 after 22 months of construction; first sample lot processed; risk production stage, recorded as pilot production; volume production scheduled for Q1 2027 (per NXP release summary). Joint venture of VIS and NXP.

fa.name: Micron HBM advanced packaging facility, Singapore

invest.label: About US$7 billion (S$9.5 billion) through the end of the decade and beyond

fa.jobs: About 1,400 initially, potentially 3,000 with expansion (per EDB summary)
fa.notes: Micron's first HBM advanced packaging facility outside Taiwan. Operations were planned for 2026 at groundbreaking; a Nov 2026 Micron statement puts initial output in early calendar 2027. A separate Singapore wafer fab (groundbreaking Jan 2026, operations 2H 2028) is mentioned in coverage but not recorded here.

fa.name: Micron Hiroshima cleanroom expansion
fa.scheme: METI subsidy up to ¥536 billion (announced 12 Sept 2025, per coverage)

invest.label: About ¥1.5 trillion (about US$9.3 billion; reported figures range $9.2–9.6 billion)

fa.capacity: Phase 1 adds about 28,000 m² of cleanroom (per coverage)
fa.notes: Largest cleanroom expansion at the site since Micron acquired Elpida in 2013 (per coverage). Equipment installation is planned from 2H 2028 (a plan, not a milestone).

fa.name: Samsung Pyeongtaek Line 4 (P4) build-out
fa.technology: DRAM (Phase 4 first, per Nov 2025 report); foundry line planned for 2026 (per same report)
fa.notes: Construction of the remaining P4 phases halted in 2024 and preparations to resume reported in mid-2025 (Korea JoongAng Daily); a Nov 2025 Korean report says Phase 4 is built first, then the postponed Phase 2. Based on press reports citing industry sources; Samsung confirmation not found in reviewed sources.

fa.name: SMIC Lingang 12-inch fab, Shanghai
partners: Lingang Free Trade Zone administration (joint venture, per coverage)
fa.notes: Construction and production status: not found in reviewed public sources. Recorded at the announcement stage only; check SMIC filings for later milestones.

fa.name: Hua Hong Wuxi 12-inch line, phase II
fa.capacity: 83,000 12-inch wafers per month (line design capacity, per report)
fa.notes: Completed and started production 10 Dec 2024, about 100 days ahead of schedule (per report). Some coverage calls this line Fab 9; that naming is not confirmed in reviewed sources. A further project, Fab 9B (RMB 3.8 billion, 55,000 wafers per month, construction completion targeted Jan 2027), is reported separately (TrendForce, Aug 2026).

fa.name: Infineon Kulim 3 SiC fab (phase 1), Kedah

invest.label: €2 billion first phase (about €5 billion more planned for phase 2)

fa.technology: 200 mm silicon carbide power semiconductors; GaN epitaxy
fa.jobs: 900 (phase 1) and 600 (phase 2) high-value jobs (per MIDA); other MIDA items cite different totals
fa.notes: First phase officially opened 8 Aug 2024 by Malaysia's Prime Minister. Phase 2 is a plan. Powered by 100% green electricity (per Infineon).

fa.name: Infineon Smart Power Fab (Module 4), Dresden
fa.scheme: German government funding approved May 2025 (per coverage)

invest.label: €5 billion, Infineon's largest single investment (per coverage)

fa.capacity: Doubles 300 mm capacity at the Dresden site (per coverage)
fa.products: Power semiconductors incl. smart power stages for AI power delivery; analog/mixed-signal
fa.notes: Opened several months ahead of schedule in early July 2026. Ramp follows demand; ramp schedule not found in reviewed sources.

fa.name: ASE Malaysia Plant 5, Penang
fa.capacity: ASE Malaysia floor space rises from about 1 million to about 3.4 million sq ft with the expansion (per coverage)
fa.technology: Packaging and test incl. advanced packaging; AIoT defect detection
fa.products: Image sensors (incl. for robots), power management chips (per Taipei Times)
fa.notes: Groundbreaking (Nov 2022) covered Plants 4 and 5. Plant 5 opened 18 Feb 2025. The advanced-packaging versus image-sensor product mix is not broken down in reviewed sources.

fa.name: SPIL P1 plant, Bandar Cassia, Penang
fa.operator: Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL), part of ASE Technology Holding
fa.technology: Wafer bumping, wafer-level chip-scale packaging, flip-chip packaging, test (planned)
fa.jobs: About 3,000 skilled jobs over 15 years (per coverage)
fa.notes: Eight-hectare site at Bandar Cassia Technology Park. Construction progress or opening not found in reviewed sources.

fa.name: Amkor Bac Ninh factory, Vietnam

invest.label: US$1.6 billion (sources differ on whether this covers the first two phases or runs to 2035)

fa.capacity: 600 million units (about 210 tonnes) a year in phase 1 per the investment certificate; phase 2 doubles output (per coverage)
fa.jobs: About 2,000 at opening; about 10,000 at full capacity (per coverage)

fa.name: Texas Instruments SM1, Sherman

invest.label: Up to about US$40 billion for the Sherman site (up to four fabs, SM1–SM4), per TI fact sheet

fa.capacity: Ramps with customer demand; ultimately tens of millions of chips a day (per TI)
fa.jobs: About 3,000 TI jobs at full build-out (per TI fact sheet)
fa.notes: Production started about three and a half years after the May 2022 groundbreaking (TI, 17 Dec 2025). Construction of the second fab, SM2, is complete (per TI); SM2 is not recorded separately.

fa.name: GlobalFoundries Malta Fab 8 expansion and second fab, New York
fa.scheme: US CHIPS and Science Act award ($1.5 billion, finalised Nov 2024); New York Green CHIPS tax credit ($575 million) (per coverage)

invest.label: More than US$11.6 billion over 10 years (NY Governor's Office)

fa.capacity: Expansion plus a new fab expected to triple Malta campus capacity over 10+ years (per coverage)
fa.technology: Automotive process technologies already used in Germany and Singapore; silicon photonics, SiGe, advanced packaging (2026 amendment)
fa.notes: In Oct 2026 Commerce agreed to amend the award, reallocating up to $955 million toward silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and advanced packaging across Malta and Burlington, Vermont, with no increase in the total (per NIST release summary). Construction start of the second fab not found in reviewed sources.

fa.name: Wolfspeed John Palmour Manufacturing Center, Siler City
fa.scheme: US CHIPS and Science Act grant (per report title)
fa.capacity: Planned to expand Wolfspeed materials capacity more than tenfold (per Wolfspeed)
fa.technology: 200 mm silicon carbide crystal growth and substrates
fa.products: SiC substrates (feeding the Mohawk Valley fab)
fa.notes: Topped out 26 Mar 2024. First 200 mm crystal furnaces switched on in June 2024 (recorded as pilot production). Axios (Feb 2025) reported the site nearing completion, with wafer production to follow. A later status was not found in reviewed sources.

pg.name: Taiwan Statute for Industrial Innovation, Article 10-2 ("Taiwan Chips Act")

facts.label: Passed
facts.value: 7 January 2023; effective 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2029 (per law-firm summary)

facts.label: Credits
facts.value: 25 % for forward-looking innovative R&D; 5 % for equipment investment (raised from 15 % for R&D)

facts.label: Equipment threshold
facts.value: Advanced-process equipment spending of at least NT$10 billion (about US$321 million) (per report)

facts.label: Eligibility
facts.value: Corporate organisations only; MOEA reviews applications (per law-firm summary)

pg.name: China National Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund, phase III ("Big Fund III")

facts.label: Fiscal support
facts.value: At least RM25 billion (about US$5.3 billion) for incentive programmes (breakdown differs across reports)

facts.label: Investment target
facts.value: At least RM500 billion in phase 1

pg.name: Vietnam semiconductor industry development strategy to 2030, vision 2050 (Decision 1018/QĐ-TTg)

facts.label: Approach
facts.value: Formula C = SET + 1 (Chip = Specialised + Electronics + Talent, plus Vietnam as a new, safe supply-chain destination)

facts.label: Phase 1 (2024–2030)
facts.value: Build human-resource base and basic capabilities in research, design, production, packaging and test (per coverage); workforce targets differ between reports and are not recorded

facts.label: Announced
facts.value: 27 July 2022; Dholera to host a 'Semicon City' (per report title)

facts.label: Capital assistance
facts.value: 40 % of the central (India Semiconductor Mission) capital assistance, disbursed over five years (per policy summaries)

facts.label: Other support
facts.value: Stamp-duty and registration-fee refund, land subsidy and utility-tariff support (per policy summaries); DLI-scheme projects not eligible
